event_name: Apollo to Artemis: To the Moon and Back Again
venue: Tim D. Lee Senior Center, Marietta
blurb:
A NASA Solar System Ambassador walking you through America's past, present, and future plans for the Moon, Mars, and beyond. That's the pitch for Tuesday afternoon at the Tim D. Lee Senior Center, and honestly it's a pretty good one.

This is a one-hour presentation covering the full arc from Apollo to the Artemis program, which is actively working to put astronauts back on the Moon. If you're the type of person who watched the documentary, or has kids who came home from school talking about Mars missions and couldn't answer their questions as well as you wanted to, this is worth the hour. A NASA Ambassador presenting locally is not something that happens every week.

Free to attend, Tuesday at 2 PM in Marietta. A smart afternoon out if you can swing it.
scoring_notes: NASA Ambassador presentations are legitimately uncommon at the local level. East Cobb's highly educated audience skews toward science and technology interest. Weekday afternoon timing limits appeal somewhat (rules out working adults, better for retirees and empty nesters with flexibility). Senior Center venue may undersell the event's broad interest potential, but the content itself is broadly appealing. Free and nearby.

blurb:
The inaugural Cumberland Art Festival lands this weekend at Galleria on the Park, presented by Genuine Parts Company, and it's a first-year event worth showing up for.

This one is brand new, which means nobody's jaded about it yet and nobody knows exactly what to expect, which is actually a reason to go. Art festivals that stick around usually stick around because the first one was worth repeating. Creativity, community, and culture in one of the more underrated green spaces in the Cumberland district. Easy to get to from East Cobb, free to walk in, and the kind of afternoon that pairs well with dinner somewhere nearby after.

Get there early, see what they built, and you'll have an opinion on it before everyone else does.
scoring_notes: Inaugural events carry natural uniqueness weight. East Cobb's educated, higher-income audience skews toward arts and culture. Cumberland/Galleria is a familiar destination for this demographic. Summary is thin so some uncertainty on programming depth, but the inaugural angle and proximity make it a solid inclusion. Free admission removes friction.

event_name: HarvestFest and Scarecrows in The Square
blurb:
Marietta Square does fall better than almost anywhere in the metro, and HarvestFest is the proof.

Saturday brings the full lineup to Glover Park: arts and crafts show, Touch-A-Truck, a costume contest, a Pie Eating Contest from Pie Bar, and the Scarecrows In The Square competition spread throughout the park. There's also a College Football watch party setup called the Big Chicken Cornerback's Coop, which is exactly as fun as it sounds. Bring your chairs and your drinks and stake out a spot.

If you've got younger kids still at home, this covers everything they want. If the kids are grown and you just want to walk the Square on a crisp October Saturday with something actually happening around you, that works too. Free to attend, easy to make a half-day of it.
scoring_notes: HarvestFest hits East Cobb's mixed family profile cleanly, activities for younger kids, atmosphere for adults, and a football watch party that bridges both groups. Marietta Square is a natural East Cobb destination. Annual event but with enough programming variety to justify inclusion. Free admission is a practical plus for families.

blurb:
Two days of smoked meat, live music, and 100-plus vendors taking over downtown Kennesaw. Thats what the Pigs & Peaches BBQ Festival brings every year, and it's right up the road.

Friday kicks things off at the United Bankshares Amphitheater at Depot Park and along Main Street. You've got established and rising musical acts, festival food from across the Southeast, drinks, shopping, and enough BBQ to make questionable decisions you won't regret. It's a full festival setup, not a food truck pop-up. If your crew hasn't been before, this is the year.

Parking is available throughout downtown Kennesaw. Free to walk in, easy to spend a few hours. Just bring a real appetite.
scoring_notes: Annual event with genuine scale (100+ vendors, multi-stage music) that plays well for established families and empty nesters alike. East Cobb is close enough to Kennesaw that it's a realistic Friday evening outing. Free admission lowers friction for groups. BBQ festival format skews broad demographic appeal. Not a one-of-a-kind event, but the scale and proximity make it worth including.

event_name: Legacy and Groove: A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire
blurb:
This show sold out last time. The Ray Howard Band is back, and if you missed the first run, here's your second chance.

Legacy and Groove is a full-band tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire, which means September, Shining Star, Got to Get You Into My Life, and the full catalog delivered with live horns, real vocals, and the kind of energy that makes it physically impossible to stay in your seat. The lobby opens at 4:30 for a silent auction benefiting the Roswell Organization for Community Development, so you get the chance to give back before the show even starts.

This is a real concert at a great venue, not background music at a festival. Roswell Cultural Arts Center keeps it intimate enough that every seat feels close. If you need a Saturday night plan that your group will still be talking about on Sunday, this is it.
scoring_notes: Earth, Wind & Fire's catalog lands squarely with the 38-55 demographic that makes up the East Cobb core. Sold-out prior run signals strong demand and adds urgency. The charity component adds meaning beyond entertainment. Roswell is a natural East Cobb adjacent destination. Strong adult couple or group night-out fit.

event_name: Strand Ole Opry: We Will Always Love Dolly
blurb:
Dolly Parton gave the world a lot. The songs, the Imagination Library, the laugh, the rhinestones. Honoring all of it in one night sounds about right.

The Strand Theatre is hosting a heartfelt tribute to Dolly's life and music on Saturday night, with community singers and a live house band working through the songs that made her legendary. Expect harmonies, sequins, and probably a few tears, because Jolene hits different when it's live. This is warm, local, and built around a woman whose music crossed every generational line.

Marietta Square on a Saturday night in October is already a great reason to get out. Add a Dolly tribute inside one of the most beautiful small theaters in the metro area and you've got a real night out. Grab your tickets and bring someone who knows every word.
scoring_notes: Dolly Parton spans generations but lands especially hard with the 38-55 crowd. The Strand is a premium local venue that East Cobb residents regularly drive to. Saturday night timing is ideal. The tribute nature of the show makes it emotionally resonant, not just a generic live music night. Strong empty nester and established family adult-night-out fit.

event_name: Mother of a Monster: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
blurb:
If you've ever been curious about where Frankenstein actually came from, not the green face paint and neck bolts version, but the real story behind one of the most haunting novels ever written, this is the night to show up.

Dr. Molly Livingston from Kennesaw State University is bringing her course on British Gothic literature to life at the William Root House on Thursday evening. She'll walk through the personal tragedies, the scientific obsessions, and the romantic idealism that pushed a teenage Mary Shelley to write a book that still defines horror and science fiction nearly 200 years later. It's a one-hour lecture, intimate and focused, and space is LIMITED.

This is the kind of thing you don't stumble into again. A historian walking you through one of literature's great origin stories, inside a 19th-century historic home, in October. The timing could not be more perfect. Don't sit on this one.
scoring_notes: East Cobb skews highly educated (65% bachelor's or higher) and 42 median age, which maps well to a literary/historical lecture. The KSU connection is local credibility. Limited space makes it genuinely can't-miss. October timing amplifies the Gothic theme. Strong adult skew is a fit for empty nesters and couples looking for a smart night out.

blurb:
There are art festivals and then there's this one: 40-plus neighbors and local artists setting up on a single block of a 1924 National Historic Register neighborhood, once a year, for one day only.

The Cherokee Heights Arts Festival is the kind of boutique show that doesn't feel like a festival at all. It feels like being invited somewhere. Original paintings, woodwork, pottery, photography, jewelry, textiles, baked goods, and more from local artists who don't sell like this anywhere else. Two music stages anchor both ends of the block with live local performances all morning and afternoon. Beer on tap. A kids' art activity from the Marietta/Cobb Museum of Art. Real holiday gifting potential if you keep your eyes open.

No admission, free parking, one mile north of the Square. It runs 9 to 4 and it only happens once a year. Saturday is genuinely the only shot.
scoring_notes: Annual one-day boutique arts festival in a historic neighborhood is a near-perfect fit for East Cobb's educated, higher-income, arts-appreciating demographic. The combination of local authenticity, free admission, live music, beer, and holiday shopping angles covers empty nesters and established families equally. One-day-only urgency is real. Proximity to Marietta Square makes it an easy yes.
